html:
In March 1797 the ship Duff landed about thirty missionaries of the London Missionary Society on Tahiti. It was the start of Protestant missions in the Pacific islands.

The society had been founded in London in 1795 by evangelical Protestants inspired by the voyages of James Cook, whose accounts made Tahiti famous in Europe. The missionaries were mostly craftsmen with little training. For years they made almost no converts, and several gave up and left during wars between Tahitian chiefs.

Their fortunes changed when the chief Pōmare II, who had lost power, turned to them. He declared himself a Christian around 1812, won back control of Tahiti in 1815, and was baptised in 1819. He set up a law code drafted with missionary help. Tahitians and other converts then carried the faith to islands across the South Pacific. Christianity became central to Polynesian life within a generation. In Hawaii a similar change began from within; see Hawaii ends the kapu.
sum: In March 1797 the ship Duff landed about thirty missionaries of the London Missionary Society on Tahiti. It was the start of Protestant missions in the Pacific islands.
